root_motivation: Recall ships an `episodic` memory kind, but nothing populates it. I write semantic+reflective memories explicitly; episodic patterns (try/fail/retry, user-redirect, tool-thrash) never land because they require an *observer*, not an author. This slice ships an end-of-session JSONL detector that surfaces the loadbearing patterns and emits candidate memories. Stop-hook integration + recall-write are downstream; this slice ends at `episode observe --dry-run <jsonl>` producing well-typed candidates a downstream writer can consume.
user_persona: Future Claude sessions on this laptop, invoked from a Stop hook after a session ends. Also: jsy manually testing detectors via `episode observe --dry-run <session.jsonl>` to see what would land in recall before wiring the hook. Pure CLI; no daemon.

acceptance_criteria.description: CLI binary `episode` accepts subcommand `observe <jsonl-path>` and parses a fixture JSONL stream of session events without panicking. Exit 0 when the fixture has no detector matches; emit nothing to stdout.

`episode observe --dry-run <jsonl-path>` emits a JSON array of candidate memories to stdout, each with `{detector, subject, body, evidence: [{session, turn, excerpt}]}`. Without `--dry-run` the CLI emits nothing on stdout (writing is downstream).
`episode detectors` lists the available detector names to stdout, one per line. At minimum: `revert`, `user-redirect`, `retry-with-tweak`. Exit 0.

The `user-redirect` detector fires when a user-role message starts with a redirect keyword (one of: `no`, `stop`, `don't`, `dont`, `actually`, `wait`) within 2 turns of an assistant-role tool-use. Produces a candidate with `detector: "user-redirect"`, the literal quote as `excerpt`, and the turn index.

The `revert` detector fires when an Edit or Write tool-use is followed within 5 turns by another Edit/Write that returns the same path's content to its pre-change state (textual revert). Produces a candidate with `detector: "revert"`, both turn indices in evidence, and the path that was reverted.

The `retry-with-tweak` detector fires when a Bash tool-use exits non-zero, followed within 3 turns by another Bash tool-use with a similar command (Jaccard token similarity ≥ 0.5 ignoring whitespace) that exits zero. Produces a candidate with `detector: "retry-with-tweak"`, both commands as evidence excerpts.

`--max-memories <N>` caps the total number of emitted candidates across all detectors. Default cap is 5. When the cap is reached the CLI stops emitting and exits 0; surplus matches are dropped silently.

Each emitted candidate's `subject` field is derived as `project:<basename of cwd>` when run from a project dir, falling back to `project:unknown` when cwd is `/` or unset. Subject is included in JSON output and is deterministic per-fixture.

Invocation errors (missing JSONL path, unreadable file, malformed CLI args) → exit code 2 with a single-line diagnostic on stderr. Malformed JSONL lines mid-stream → skip the line, log to stderr, continue.
Idempotency: running `episode observe --dry-run <fixture>` twice produces byte-identical stdout. Ordering of candidates is deterministic (sorted by detector name, then turn index).

scope: Rust 2024 CLI crate `episodic-observer` producing an `episode` binary.
Streaming JSONL parser over Claude Code session journals.
Three Phase-0 detectors: revert, user-redirect, retry-with-tweak.
Candidate emission as JSON array (--dry-run) or via stdout (no-op for now; writer integration is downstream).
Deterministic output ordering for repeatable testing.
Acceptance + proptest fixtures committed under tests/fixtures/.
non_goals: No Stop-hook installation in this slice (the hook script is one line; lives outside autobuilder).
No `recall write` integration in this slice (writer is downstream — observe emits candidates; another tool consumes).
No content-analysis of code changes (detectors look at session-event structure, not code semantics).
No editorial framing — detector output preserves literal quotes/excerpts; no LLM-generated rephrasing.
No cross-session correlation (this slice sees one JSONL per invocation).

five_whys_trace.q: Why an end-of-session observer rather than PostToolUse instrumentation?
five_whys_trace.a: PostToolUse fires per turn and can't see the *arc* of an attempt (try/fail/retry needs lookahead). Stop sees the whole session as a finite document; patterns are detectable in one pass.

five_whys_trace.q: Why ship Phase 0 as `--dry-run` only (no recall write)?
five_whys_trace.a: Detector quality matters more than wiring. Manual `--dry-run` runs against real session JSONLs let me tune detector thresholds before any memory ever lands in recall. Wiring is mechanical; tuning is the load-bearing work.

five_whys_trace.q: Why three detectors (revert, user-redirect, retry-with-tweak) instead of all six from the PRD?
five_whys_trace.a: These three have the cleanest event shape (single tool-use pair or single user-message check). The other three (tool-thrash, skill-rejected, successful-novelty) require richer state or file-system inspection — better to ship the easy three first and iterate.

Detectors are heuristic. Unbounded emission risks filling the memory store with noise per session. Five episodic memories per session is enough to cover the loadbearing patterns; more is over-fitting on a single day's pathology.
Episodic memories about coding work are most useful scoped to a project. Pattern: 'when working on autobuilder, I tried X and X failed' is more recallable than the same fact filed under subject:self.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Are 'revert' detections only edits to the same path, or also cross-path semantic reverts?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Same-path textual reverts only in this slice. Cross-path semantic reverts are too speculative for a syntactic detector.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What's the similarity threshold for `retry-with-tweak`?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Jaccard token similarity ≥ 0.5 (ignoring whitespace). Tunable later; this lets `cargo test foo` → `cargo test foo --release` match without matching `cargo test` → `git log`.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What format do session JSONLs take?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Claude Code's session.jsonl — newline-delimited JSON, one event per line, with fields `type`, `role`, `content`, `tool_calls` (varies by version). The parser is best-effort: any line that parses to an object is included; non-object lines are skipped with stderr.
